Interop Resolution Service

API reference for Onyx: member resolution, POST /v1/resolve.

Version v1 · Point32Health · the OpenAPI document (YAML and JSON) that ships with this page carries the same contract.

1 Overview

Member resolution for Onyx, POST /v1/resolve: resolves an EMR-supplied member id against the plan's member records, reports whether coverage is active on the date of service, and returns the id as resolved and in every UM vendor's format, each with the payer for that vendor's request. Every answer travels in an envelope: data and header.

One call per prior authorization. Send the member id exactly as the provider's EMR supplied it, the date of service (or the period of service) and, when known, the patient's date of birth. The answer says whether the member was found, whether coverage is active on that date, the line of business to route on, and the member id in every UM vendor's format with the payer to put on that vendor's request.

Base URL and access. The base URL is issued by Point32Health for each environment and is not part of this document; the path below is relative to it. Authentication is OAuth 2.0: work with Point32Health to obtain the client credentials and the token endpoint for each environment, and send the access token on every call in the Authorization header. Nothing in the body or the path carries a credential. A rejected or expired token is answered in front of the service (401 or 403) without the envelope of section 2.

2 The operation and the envelope

POST /v1/resolve with Content-Type: application/json. The service always answers JSON, whatever Accept header is sent.

Finds the member behind the id the EMR typed, says whether coverage is active on the date of service (or on every day of a period of service), and returns the id as resolved and in every configured UM vendor's format (memberId.forVendors), each entry with the payer for that vendor's request (payerId, payerName). When several members on the plan match and no dateOfBirth settles it, the outcome is AMBIGUOUS and the message says what to resend; the other members are never listed. clientId, clientType (EXT or INT), requestId and memberId are required; unknown properties are ignored. A sent date is the date evaluated; an unusable date is a 400. POST because the member id is PHI and must not appear in URLs; the operation is a pure read and may be repeated.

The envelope

Every answer, success or error, is one JSON object with two members: data and header. On a success, data is the member resolution answer of section 4. On an error, data holds the error details of section 6. header is the same on both:

FieldTypeRequiredMeaning
header.httpStatusintegeryesThe HTTP status of the answer, the same value as on the wire
header.messagestringyesA short text about the answer; on an error it may repeat the code
header.statussuccess | erroryessuccess or error
header.statusCodestringOn an error only: the error code to branch on (the catalog in the reference page)
header.timestampinteger (epoch ms)yesWhen the answer was produced, milliseconds since 1970-01-01 UTC

The HTTP status on the wire and header.httpStatus always agree; branch on either. On an error, header.statusCode is the error code to branch on and header.status is error.

Headers

HeaderDirectionRule
X-Correlation-IdinOptional transport-level id, 1 to 64 characters of letters, digits, ., _, : or -; opaque. Missing or invalid: the service generates one. The caller's own id for the call is requestId in the body.
X-Correlation-IdoutThe echoed or generated value, for support.
Retry-AfteroutOn 503, when present: seconds to wait before retrying; 10 when the header is absent.

Responses

StatusMeaning
200outcome ACTIVE | INACTIVE | NOT_FOUND | AMBIGUOUS; memberId.forVendors, each vendor with its payer, present for ACTIVE and INACTIVE
400INVALID_REQUEST for a missing or unusable clientId, clientType or requestId, a missing memberId, an unusable date or a body that is not JSON; MEMBER_LOOKUP_REJECTED when the member lookup answered 400 (data.details[0].code HTTP_400, the lookup's text in the message)
422DOB_MISMATCH: the date of birth matches no record for this id
404INVALID_REQUEST / ROUTE_NOT_FOUND: wrong path; a connector defect (a member that is not found is a 200 with outcome NOT_FOUND)
405INVALID_REQUEST / METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED: the operation is POST only
415INVALID_REQUEST / UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE: the request body must be application/json
502MEMBER_LOOKUP_ERROR or MEMBER_LOOKUP_INVALID_RESPONSE (the member lookup); MEMBER_PLAN_ERROR or MEMBER_PLAN_INVALID_RESPONSE (the member plan lookup)
503MEMBER_LOOKUP_UNAVAILABLE or MEMBER_PLAN_UNAVAILABLE; retry after the Retry-After seconds; header Retry-After (Seconds to wait before retrying, when present (10 otherwise))
500INTERNAL_ERROR: the service itself failed; retry once later, then alert the service owners with the correlationId and requestId

3 Request

Member resolution request: clientId, clientType, requestId and memberId are required; unknown properties are ignored; a sent date must be usable. Unknown properties are ignored, so a vendor sent by habit does no harm: the answer is always for every vendor.

FieldTypeRequiredMeaning
clientIdstringyesThe calling system, as registered with the plan: letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-', at most 50 characters
clientTypeEXT | INTyesEXT for a caller outside the plan, INT for an internal one
requestIdstringyesThe caller's id for this call, unique per request; echoed in the response and in every error response. Letters, digits, '.', '_', ':' or '-', at most 64 characters
memberIdstringyesThe member id exactly as the EMR supplied it. Looked up unchanged (surrounding whitespace removed); the service never checks its shape, length or characters. For instance a THP Medicare card number is a letter and 8 digits; the example is that pattern, masked
dateOfServicestringDate of service, yyyy-MM-dd; the first date when the service covers a period. Omitted, null or blank: today in US Eastern time (America/New_York) is used, dateOfServiceDefaulted is true and the answer's dateOfService says which date was used; send the date whenever you have it. A sent value is the date evaluated: any future date is judged on the coverage on record; not a real date (DATE_OF_SERVICE_INVALID), or more than 10 years back (DATE_OF_SERVICE_OUT_OF_RANGE), is a 400.
dateOfServiceEndstringOptional last date of service, yyyy-MM-dd, when the service covers a period: coverage must hold on every day from dateOfService to it. Not before dateOfService; needs dateOfService. Omitted, null or blank counts as not sent.
dateOfBirthstringOptional patient date of birth, yyyy-MM-dd, used only to verify the member or to tell apart the members on a plan who share the id. Omitted, null or blank counts as not sent. Not a real date is a 400 (DATE_OF_BIRTH_INVALID); in the future or more than 125 years ago is a 400 (DATE_OF_BIRTH_OUT_OF_RANGE). Never logged, never echoed.

4 Response (200)

The answer: the outcome Onyx branches on, one sentence for a person, the member id as received, as resolved and in every vendor's format with that vendor's payer, the line of business, the date evaluated, the coverage flag with its period, the caller's requestId and a traceId for support. A field that does not apply is absent, never null. The answer is the data member of the envelope; fields are sent in the order listed. Lists of values marked "for example" are not closed: new vendors and new lines of business can be added, so never reject a value that is not in this document.

FieldTypeRequiredMeaning
dataobjectyesThe answer: the outcome Onyx branches on, one sentence for a person, the member id as received, as resolved and in every vendor's format with that vendor's payer, the line of business, the date evaluated, the coverage flag with its period, the caller's requestId and a traceId for support. A field that does not apply is absent, never null
data.outcomeACTIVE | INACTIVE | NOT_FOUND | AMBIGUOUSyesACTIVE: member found, coverage active on the date of service (or on every day of the period). INACTIVE: member found, not covered on that date or not on every day of the period; message says why. NOT_FOUND: no member for this id on that date. AMBIGUOUS: several members match and nothing sent tells them apart; message says what to resend
data.messagestringyesOne sentence for a person reading the answer. Branch on outcome, not on this text
data.memberIdobjectyesThe member id as received, as resolved, and in every vendor's format
data.memberId.receivedstringyesThe member id as sent, surrounding whitespace removed
data.memberId.resolvedstringThe id the lookup resolved to, as the plan stores it; for a converted member a different number from the one received. Present on ACTIVE and INACTIVE answers only
data.memberId.forVendors[]arrayThe resolved id in every configured vendor's format, each with the payer for that vendor's request; one entry per vendor, sorted by vendor code. Present on ACTIVE and INACTIVE answers only
data.memberId.forVendors[].vendorstringThe vendor code, for example EVICORE; today CARELON, EVICORE, EVOLENT, MHK, ONYX and OPTUM. Vendors can be added, so never treat the list as closed
data.memberId.forVendors[].memberIdstringThe resolved id in this vendor's format: the member id to put on this vendor's request
data.memberId.forVendors[].payerIdstringThe payer id to put on this vendor's request; it differs by vendor and by the member's heritage company, so use the entry's value as given
data.memberId.forVendors[].payerNamestringThe payer name that goes with payerId
data.lineOfBusinessstringThe line of business Onyx routes on, from the plan in effect on the date of service, for example SCO, MA-HMO, MA-PPO, D-SNP, MA-TOGETHER, RI-TOGETHER or MA-QHP; values can be added, so never treat the list as closed. When no rule applies, the member record's own category is passed through (for example MCR, PP, COM), and the field is absent when the record carries none. Present on ACTIVE and INACTIVE answers only. Agree with Point32Health how to route a value outside the list, or an absent one
data.dateOfServicedate (yyyy-MM-dd)yesThe date evaluated; the first date when a period was asked about
data.dateOfServiceEnddate (yyyy-MM-dd)The last date evaluated; present only when the request asked about a period
data.dateOfServiceDefaultedbooleanyestrue when no dateOfService was sent and today was used
data.coverageobjectThe coverage flag and the coverage period behind it. Present on ACTIVE and INACTIVE answers only
data.coverage.coverageIdstringAn id for the coverage period: the resolved id reduced to letters and digits, then the effective and end dates as yyyyMMdd, run together with no separator (39991231 for an open-ended period). Present whenever the dates are; the same member with the same coverage always gets the same value
data.coverage.activebooleanyesThe flag: true when coverage holds on the date of service, or on every day of the period of service
data.coverage.effectiveDatedate (yyyy-MM-dd)First day of the coverage period
data.coverage.endDatedate (yyyy-MM-dd)Last day of the coverage period; 3999-12-31 for an open-ended period
data.requestIdstringyesThe caller's requestId, echoed
data.traceIdstringyesThe id of the member lookup behind this answer; quote it to support
data.sourceMessageobjectWhat the member lookup said when it had no member for the id. NOT_FOUND only, and only when the lookup sent a message
data.sourceMessage.typestringThe message type as the lookup sent it
data.sourceMessage.statusstringThe status as the lookup sent it
data.sourceMessage.codestringThe message code as the lookup sent it
data.sourceMessage.textstringThe message text as the lookup sent it
headerobjectyesThe envelope header on every answer
header.httpStatusintegeryesThe HTTP status of the answer, the same value as on the wire
header.messagestringyesA short text about the answer; on an error it may repeat the code
header.statussuccess | erroryessuccess or error
header.statusCodestringOn an error only: the error code to branch on (the catalog in the reference page)
header.timestampinteger (epoch ms)yesWhen the answer was produced, milliseconds since 1970-01-01 UTC

An AMBIGUOUS answer never lists the members who share the id.

5 What to do with each answer

Onyx branches on data.outcome for a 200, and on the HTTP status (or header.httpStatus) otherwise. Two rules for every row: Onyx never reformats a member id itself when the service is up, and Onyx keeps the full response with its transaction.

SignalMeaningOnyx action
200 ACTIVEMember found; coverage active on the date of service, or on every day of the period of service (data.coverage.active is true).Send each vendor its data.memberId.forVendors entry: the memberId of the entry whose vendor is that vendor, already in the vendor's format, with that entry's payerId and payerName on the request. Route on data.lineOfBusiness. Keep data.coverage.coverageId with the transaction as the reference to the coverage period behind the decision.
200 INACTIVEMember found; not covered on that date, or not on every day of the period. data.message says why.Hold for intake. data.memberId.forVendors and data.lineOfBusiness are still there if the business rule says to submit anyway.
200 NOT_FOUNDNo member for this id on that date. data.sourceMessage carries what the member lookup said, when it sent a message."Member not found" worklist. If Onyx holds a fuller form of the id (for instance with the suffix), one resend with it.
200 AMBIGUOUSSeveral members on the plan share the id and nothing sent tells them apart. Nobody is listed.One resend with dateOfBirth or the member's full id including the suffix. If it is still AMBIGUOUS (twins share a date of birth, or the records carry none), intake takes the full id from the member's card and resends.
400 / 422Request or identity problem (the error catalog below).Never retry. Route by header.statusCode and data.details[].code.
502 / 503 / 500A lookup behind the service, or the service itself, could not answer.Retry as section 8 says, always with a new requestId; when the retries are used up, park the transaction and alert the service owners.
401 / 403 / 429Answered by the API gateway in front of the service, without the envelope of section 2.401 and 403: a token problem; obtain a fresh token, never retry the same one. 429: treat like a 503 and retry after its Retry-After.
No response at all (connection refused, timeout)The service is down or unreachable.Retry once with a new requestId, as section 8 says; still no response: pass the member id to the UM vendor exactly as the EMR supplied it, and record the requestId so the transaction can be reconciled later.

6 Errors

Every non-200 answer produced by the service is the envelope of section 2 with header.status error, the error code in header.statusCode and the details in data.details. Answers produced by the API gateway in front of it (401, 403, 429, or any response whose body is not JSON) do not carry the envelope: treat 401 and 403 as a token problem and never retry the same token; treat 429 like a 503 and retry after its Retry-After. header.statusCode is stable and is what to branch on; data.details[].code refines it; data.requestId echoes the caller's id whenever it was usable, so a 400 about another field still carries it, and is an empty string otherwise; data.traceId is present once the member lookup was made.

FieldTypeRequiredMeaning
dataobjectyesThe data part of an error answer
data.requestIdstringyesThe caller's requestId when the request carried a usable one, else an empty string
data.traceIdstringThe id of the member lookup behind the answer, present once the lookup was made
data.details[]arrayyesOne entry per problem found; every problem with a request is reported together
data.details[].codestringyesThe detail code that refines error.code, for example MEMBER_ID_MISSING, DATE_OF_SERVICE_INVALID, HTTP_400, READ_TIMEOUT
data.details[].fieldstringThe request field the problem is about, when there is one
data.details[].messagestringyesOne sentence for a person
headerobjectyesThe envelope header on every answer
header.httpStatusintegeryesThe HTTP status of the answer, the same value as on the wire
header.messagestringyesA short text about the answer; on an error it may repeat the code
header.statussuccess | erroryessuccess or error
header.statusCodestringOn an error only: the error code to branch on (the catalog in the reference page)
header.timestampinteger (epoch ms)yesWhen the answer was produced, milliseconds since 1970-01-01 UTC

8 Timeouts, retries, security

  • Timeouts. A successful answer normally takes well under a second. When a lookup behind the service cannot answer, the failure is reported within about 15 seconds; set the client timeout above that.
  • Retry policy. 503: wait the Retry-After seconds (10 when the header is absent) and retry; the number of attempts is to be agreed with Point32Health (three until then). 502 and 500: retry once. No response at all (connection refused, timeout): retry once. Never retry a 400 or 422, and never retry a 401 or 403 with the same token. Every retry carries a new requestId. When the retries are used up: for 502, 503 and 500, park the transaction and alert the service owners with the requestId and the X-Correlation-Id; for no response at all, pass the member id to the UM vendor exactly as the EMR supplied it and record the requestId so the transaction can be reconciled later.
  • Security. OAuth 2.0 access tokens, issued per environment by Point32Health, on every call; certificates and rate limits are handled by the API gateway in front of the service. The member id and date of birth are PHI: send them in the body only, never in a URL, and do not log the date of birth.
  • Caller identification. Onyx sends clientId ONYX and clientType EXT on every call, and a new requestId per call; support finds a call by that requestId or by the traceId in the answer.
